title: Electrospun PLA: How Surface Treatment Changed the Experiment
license: CC BY 4.0, 2020 authors / Surface & Coatings Technology
source_visual_limits: Actual 2020 electrospun PLA fibre-mat study; Figure 1, original SEM Figure 5, AFM Figure 6, FTIR Figure 7 and Table 3. No figures from the separate 2021 PLA foil/aluminium adhesion experiment.
human_review: NOT APPROVED — study figure crop review, pronunciation and rights attribution remain
narrator: Kokoro ONNX, synthetic, not a real researcher narration

headline: A FIBRE MAT.
NOT A FILM.
chapters.narration: This is an electrospun PLA scaffold, not a packaging film. The question was whether a carefully modified surface could reduce bacterial colonization without losing its fibrous architecture.

headline: ELECTRIC
FIELD → FIBRES
chapters.narration: Electrospinning turns a polymer solution into fine fibres. The source paper used a high voltage needle and a collecting drum. This moving strand is an explanatory schematic, not filmed laboratory footage.

headline: THIRTY SECONDS
OF PLASMA
chapters.narration: A brief radiofrequency plasma treatment generated reactive surface sites. Thirty seconds was selected for subsequent grafting after the authors examined wettability and hydroperoxide formation.

headline: THE FIBRES
ARE REAL
chapters.narration: The original scanning electron micrographs show the untreated mat, plasma treated fibres and both acid grafted preparations. These are the images of this scaffold experiment, with its own three micrometre scale bars.

headline: SURFACE
TOPOGRAPHY
chapters.narration: Atomic force microscopy revealed differences in surface roughness and morphology after treatment. These are the actual five sample conditions reported in Figure six, not illustrations borrowed from a different polymer study.

headline: LOOK AT
THE SPECTRA
chapters.narration: The original FTIR spectra compare untreated, plasma treated and acid grafted PLA. Band changes support surface modification but cannot, on their own, establish the complete mechanism.

headline: BACTERIAL
COLONIES
chapters.narration: Table three reports zero colonies for both grafted fibre mats in all three entries for each tested bacterium. These are laboratory assessment scores, not clinical infection outcomes.

headline: THE CLAIM
HAS LIMITS
chapters.eyebrow: SURFACE SCIENCE / NOT A CLINICAL IMPLANT
chapters.narration: The paper links surface treatment to measurable fibre properties and lower bacterial growth in vitro. It does not establish long term safety or effectiveness after implantation.

original_figures: Figures 1/5/6/7 and ORIGINAL Table 3 of the 2020 scaffold study
distinction: Do not use separate 2021 PLA film-aluminium peel experiment
